diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume $B$ is a matrix, and let $x$, $y$, and $b$ be three vectors, such that $x \in \spand(B^{\perp})$, and $b=(x+y)\gamma$, where $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$
we provide general bounds on the growth of the condition number as columns are added to a matrix without making any assumptions about the matrix or the added column

issues.failure_explanation: The Gram matrix [B,(x+y)gamma]^T[B,(x+y)gamma] has bottom-right entry gamma^2*||x+y||^2 (third quote). The proof then rewrites it as diag(B^TB,1) + [[0,gamma*B^T y],[gamma*y^T B, gamma^2*||x+y||^2]] (second quote); this sum has bottom-right entry 1+gamma^2*||x+y||^2, so the identity is false (a spurious +1) and all subsequent eigenvalue bounds (Lemma lm:rank2 plus Weyl-type inequalities) are derived for the wrong matrix. Hence item 1 is false: with B=[e1,e2] in R^3, x=0.5*e3, y=0, gamma=1 the true kappa([B,b])=2 while the bound gives sqrt(2.5/2)=1.118; with x=0, y=e1 the added column lies in span(B), so [B,b] is singular (kappa infinite) while the bound is 2.618. Item 2 is also false (same B, x=0, y=e1, eps=2.5 satisfies ||B^T y||/||x+y||=1 <= (eps^2-1)/4=1.3125, yet the claimed bound is finite). Secondary gaps in the same proof: lambda_max/min of diag(B^TB,1) is replaced by sigma_max/min(B)^2, requiring sigma_max(B)>=1>=sigma_min(B), not assumed; and item 2's hypothesis does not imply the sqrt(1+4||B^T y||^2/||x+y||^2)<=eps needed in the proof once eps>sqrt(5).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must use the correct decomposition diag(B^TB,0)+[[0,gamma*B^T y],[gamma*y^T B,gamma^2*||x+y||^2]] (which by itself yields only a vacuous lower bound on sigma_min) and must add hypotheses excluding added columns with a non-negligible component in span(B) (e.g. ||B^T y||_2 small relative to sigma_min(B)*||x+y||_2) and rederive the sigma_min lower bound, since under no assumptions kappa([B,b]) is unbounded (b in span(B) makes [B,b] singular) while the stated bound stays finite.
issues.overall_effect: Both items of Section 3's main theorem, the advertised 'under no assumption' extension of Liesen et al. and the corresponding abstract claim, are unreliable. No later labelled result cites thm:cool.
issues.title: Theorem thm:cool is false: proof uses a Gram-matrix decomposition with a spurious +1, and both item bounds fail
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false in its advertised 'no assumption' regime; every repair either excludes regimes via new hypotheses or collapses the sigma_min lower bound to a vacuous one, so no comparable version of the primary claim survives without a new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Letting alpha->0 in the stated integral definition (using I_{M-1}(t) ~ (t/2)^{M-1}/Gamma(M)) gives Q^ma_M(0,beta) = Gamma(M, beta^2/2)/Gamma(M); for instance Q^ma_1(0,beta) = e^{-beta^2/2}. The stated closed form Gamma(M,beta^2)/Gamma(M) (which gives e^{-beta^2}) is inconsistent with the definition's own integral by a factor 2 in the threshold argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace beta^2 by beta^2/2 in the alpha=0 formula, i.e. Q^ma_M(0,beta) = Gamma(M, beta^2/2)/Gamma(M).
issues.overall_effect: Any numerical evaluation of Q^ma at alpha=0 via the stated closed form (as would be natural in Corollaries cor:golden2 and cor:golden3) is off by a factor-2 rescaling of the threshold; the closed form is unusable as stated, although the symbolic theorems remain correct under the integral definition and their proofs bypass this clause.
issues.title: Marcum-Q definition's alpha=0 closed form contradicts its own integral definition (missing factor 1/2)
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction restores internal consistency of the definition; no theorem's statement or proof depends on the erroneous closed form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: as the dimensions of \( Q^{\perp} \) and \( Q \) are \( m-n \) and \( n \), respectively

issues.failure_explanation: X-bar (the coordinates of X in the m-n columns of Q-perp, and itself never defined before use) lies in R^{m-n} whereas X lies in R^m, and the index range 1..n is wrong as well; the componentwise identity X-bar_i = X_i is impossible unless n=0. The fact the proof actually needs, ||X-bar||_2 = ||X||_2 (isometry of Q-perp), is true but is not what is asserted, so the final application of Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel in R^{m-n} is unjustified as written.

failure_location.quote: Since \( X \in \text{span}(Q^{\perp}) \), then \( \bar{X}_i = X_i \) for \( 1 \leq i \leq n \).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sentence by the isometry argument: X = Q-perp * X-bar with Q-perp having orthonormal columns, hence ||X-bar||_2 = ||X||_2, and apply thm:Malcum-Bessel to X-bar + Y-bar in R^{m-n}.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:projected-noise is invalid as written, though its stated conclusion is correct; downstream results (cor:golden3, thm:noise-ls, cor-main, cor:added-2) use only the true conclusion.
issues.title: Proof of thm:projected-noise justifies its key step by a dimensionally invalid component identity
issues.why_classification: One false proof step with a routine local repair; the conclusion and all uses of the theorem survive.

issues.failure_explanation: P_B^perp projects onto (span B)^perp, of dimension m - rank(B), so ||P_B^perp(Y)||^2/sigma^2 is chi-squared with m - rank(B) degrees of freedom, while the stated formula uses m-n. For rank-deficient B (e.g. B = 0_{m x n} with m >= n >= 1) the two sides involve chi^2_m versus chi^2_{m-n} and differ; for m = n with full rank the order (m-n)/2 = 0 lies outside the definition's range M > 0. The corollary is stated with no proof and without the full-column-rank hypothesis that the paper states explicitly elsewhere (thm:noise-ls, cor-main).

failure_location.quote: Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \), and \( Y \in \mathbb{R}^m \) be a random vector with i.i.d. components \( Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2) \). Then:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that B has full column rank (and m > n); the formula then follows from thm:projected-noise applied with an orthonormal basis of span(B).
issues.overall_effect: cor:golden3 gives wrong probabilities for rank-deficient B and is undefined at m = n.
issues.title: cor:golden3 is false for rank-deficient B (and undefined when m=n)
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis restores the claim; the only in-paper use (thm:noise-ls's proof) applies it to a full-rank orthonormal Q.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The probability that the norm of \( X + P_{Q}^{\perp}(Y) \) exceeds \( \varepsilon \) is given by \( \mathcal{Q}^{ma}_{(m-n)/2}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2}{\sigma},\frac{\varepsilon}{\sigma}\right) \)

issues.failure_explanation: By thm:projected-noise the probability equals Q^ma_{(m-n)/2}(||X||_2/sigma, 25.6), which depends on ||X||_2. The assumptions of thm:projected-noise allow X = 0, for which the probability is P(chi^2_{>=100} > 655.36) < 10^-80, not >= 0.9734. The claim only becomes plausible with a lower bound on ||X||_2 (e.g. ||X||_2 = 1, where the probability is essentially 1); no such hypothesis is stated and no proof is given.

failure_location.quote: Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:projected-noise}, with \( m-n \geq 100 \), \( \sigma = 2^{-8} \), and \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{10} \), we have:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis fixing ||X||_2 (e.g. ||X||_2 = 1, for which the stated lower bound holds easily) or restate the probability as a function of ||X||_2.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's numerical claim (probability >= 0.9734) is false as stated.
issues.title: cor:added-1 is false: the probability depends on ||X||_2, which the assumptions leave unconstrained
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis addition preserves the corollary's message; no downstream result uses it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $Z_1 \sim \chi^2_n$, $Z_2 \sim \chi'^2_{m-n}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2^2}{\sigma^2}\right)$, therefore, by Chapter 6, equation 40 of \cite{patnaik1949non}, we have:

issues.failure_explanation: Z_1 = ||P_Q Y||_2 and Z_2 = ||X + P_{Q^perp} Y||_2 are chi-distributed norms (Z_1^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_n, Z_2^2/sigma^2 ~ noncentral chi^2_{m-n}), consistent with the proof's own Marcum-Q displays; the assertion 'Z_1 ~ chi^2_n, Z_2 ~ chi'^2' is false, so the ratio of norms Z_2/(m-n) over Z_1/n is not noncentral F. The event ||r|| >= 1/sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) is equivalent to (Z_2^2/(m-n))/(Z_1^2/n) >= n*eps_2^2/((m-n)*eps_1^2), so the correct argument is n*eps_2^2/((m-n)*eps_1^2), not n*eps_2/((m-n)*eps_1). Counterexample: m=2, n=1, X=0, eps_1=2, eps_2=1: the left side is P(||r|| >= 1/sqrt(5)) = 0.705 (Beta(1/2,1/2) tail) while the stated right side (survival of F(1,1) at 1/2) is 0.608. The paper also never defines whether F' denotes a CDF or a survival function; the proof's chain requires the survival reading, and even then the argument misses the squares.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the proof to apply the noncentral-F distribution to Z_2^2/Z_1^2 (defining F' as the survival function of the noncentral F), and replace the argument by n*eps_2^2/((m-n)*eps_1^2) in thm:noise-ls and in the dependent corollaries.
issues.overall_effect: The exact probability identity of thm:noise-ls, and the probability guarantees repeated with the same unsquared argument in cor-main and cor:added-2, are wrong for generic eps_1/eps_2.
issues.title: thm:noise-ls states the wrong noncentral-F argument: the norms Z1, Z2 are conflated with chi-squared variables (missing squares)
issues.why_classification: The section's main distributional identity is false and propagates into two corollaries' probability guarantees, but the repair is contained (insert squares, fix the two false distributional assertions) and preserves the form of every guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: sigma_max(diag(R,gamma)) = max(sigma_max(R), |gamma|), so the proof's step (and items 1 and the second form of 3) is valid only for gamma >= 0; the hypothesis gamma > 0 (used by the underlying Theorem 2.3 of Liesen et al.) is omitted. For gamma < 0, max{sigma_max(B),gamma} = sigma_max(B) and max{kappa(B),||B||_2/gamma, gamma*||B^dagger||_2} = kappa(B), which are too small: with m=3, B=[e1,e2], c=e3, gamma=-10 one gets sigma_max([B,c*gamma]) = 10 > 1 = max{sigma_max(B),gamma}*sigma_max([Q,c]) and kappa([B,c*gamma]) = 10 > kappa(B)*kappa([Q,c]) = 1.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume gamma > 0 (or replace gamma by |gamma| throughout items 1-3).
issues.overall_effect: Items 1 and 3 are false on the negative-gamma half of the stated parameter range (item 2 is vacuously true there; lm:cond-ls uses item 3's first form, which is valid for all gamma != 0).
issues.title: thm:min-max-cond items 1 and 3 fail for negative gamma (missing gamma>0 hypothesis)
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition (gamma > 0, as in the cited theorem) fixes the regime; all intended uses take gamma > 0.

issues.failure_explanation: The two displayed expressions are different functions of (B,c,gamma) and are not equal in general, even for gamma > 0. Counterexample: m=3, B=[e1,e2], c=e1+e3, gamma=2 gives max{kappa(B),||B||_2,||B^dagger||_2}*kappa([Q,c*gamma]) = 4.27 while max{kappa(B),||B||_2/gamma,gamma*||B^dagger||_2}*kappa([Q,c]) = 5.24. Both are valid upper bounds on kappa([B,c*gamma]) (= 4.27 here), but the asserted equality is false; moreover the proof derives only the second bound (quoted), so the first inequality is stated without support (it is true, via [B,c*gamma] = [Q,c*gamma]diag(R,1)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false equality and state the two bounds separately, adding the one-line factorization [B,c*gamma] = [Q,c*gamma]diag(R,1) to establish the first form.
issues.overall_effect: Item 3's displayed chain is false as stated; a reader substituting between the two forms obtains wrong values.
issues.title: Item 3 of thm:min-max-cond asserts a false equality between its two bound expressions
issues.why_classification: Local restructuring; both endpoint bounds remain true and the in-paper use (lm:cond-ls uses the first form) survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $r \neq 0$ is the residual of the least squares problem ($\|r\|_2 = \min_{u} \|c - Bu\|_2$)

issues.failure_explanation: The invoked Theorem 2.3 of [liesen2002least] (restated as thm:strak) assumes gamma > 0 and takes r as the residual of the unscaled c (||r||_2 = min_u ||c - Bu||_2). With the statement's definition ||r||_2 = min_z ||c*gamma - Bz||_2 = gamma * min_z ||c - Bz||_2, the displayed bound is wrong for gamma != 1: for m=3, B=[e1,e2], c=e1+0.5*e3, gamma=2 it gives (6+sqrt(20))/4 = 2.62 while kappa([B,2c]) = 5.83; for c=e3, gamma=2 the radicand alpha^2 - 4*gamma^2*||r||^2 = 25-64 is negative, so the bound is not even real. For gamma < 0 the right-hand side is negative while kappa >= 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define ||r||_2 = min_z ||c - Bz||_2 (residual of the unscaled column) and assume gamma > 0, matching thm:strak; equivalently, rescale the formula to (alpha + sqrt(alpha^2 - 4||r||_2^2))/(2||r||_2) for the scaled residual.
issues.overall_effect: lm:cond-ls is false or ill-posed outside gamma = 1; its downstream cor:cond-ls (which sets gamma = 1, where the two residual definitions coincide) is unaffected.
issues.title: lm:cond-ls defines r as the residual of c*gamma, making its bound false for gamma != 1 (and for gamma < 0)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the setup versus the invoked theorem; the gamma = 1 case used downstream is correct as is.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 -  \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$, and then applying Corollary \ref{cor:cond-ls} and Theorem \ref{thm:noise-ls}.
Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \) with columns of norm 1, \( q\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), such that \( \|q\|_2=1 \).

issues.failure_explanation: First, q is never defined in cor-main (the reading consistent with the cited results is q = (X+Y)/||X+Y||_2). Second, the proof applies cor:cond-ls, which requires B to have unit-norm columns, but cor-main assumes only full rank; the conclusion is false without unit columns even with a corrected constant (m=3, B = 0.001*[e1,e2], X=e3, sigma -> 0: kappa([B,q]) ~ 1000 while kappa(B) = 1 and any order-1 constant times kappa(B) fails, with the claimed probability ~ 1). Third, carrying out the proof (g(t) = (1+sqrt(1-t^2))/t decreasing, ||r|| >= 1/sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) from thm:noise-ls) yields the constant sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) + eps_1/eps_2, not eps_1*sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2); the stated constant is smaller and the claim is false for small eps_1 (e.g. eps_1 = 0.05, eps_2 = 0.5, B orthonormal, ||X|| large: the claimed probability is ~ 1 but the claimed bound ~ 0.05*kappa(B) < 1 <= kappa([B,q])).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define q = (X+Y)/||X+Y||_2, add the hypothesis that B has unit-norm columns, and replace the constant by sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) + eps_1/eps_2 (the stated eps_1*sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) is valid only for eps_1 >= 2); propagate the corrected constant to cor:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's headline guarantee (constant and probability) is false over a broad parameter regime and its statement is incomplete; cor:added-2's product bound inherits the false constant.
issues.title: cor-main: q is undefined, the unit-column hypothesis required by cor:cond-ls is missing, and the stated growth constant is false
issues.why_classification: A contained repair (define q, add the standard unit-column hypothesis, rederive the constant) preserves the result's form and the downstream product bound, but the stated guarantee is mathematically false over a regime and must be rederived rather than patched.

issues.failure_explanation: At step i the matrix of already computed columns has i-1 columns, so applying cor-main (whose probability is F'_{m-n,n}(n*eps_2/((m-n)*eps_1); ||X||^2/sigma^2) with n existing columns) yields F'_{m-i+1, i-1}((i-1)*eps_2/((m-i+1)*eps_1); ||a_i||^2/sigma^2); the stated F'_{m-i,i}(i*eps_2/((m-i)*eps_1); ...) has both the degrees of freedom and the multipliers off by one (and is undefined at i = n when m = n). Moreover, cor-main's hypotheses fix B and X, but here B = Q-hat[:,1:i-1] and a_i are random (a_i is required to lie in the random subspace span(Q-hat[:,1:i-1])^perp), so the noncentrality ||a_i||^2/sigma^2 inside the stated probability is itself random and the probability is not well-defined as written; the proof applies cor-main without any conditioning argument and uses the undefined symbol w_i.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the indices to F'_{m-i+1, i-1} with argument (i-1)*eps_{2,i}^2/((m-i+1)*eps_{1,i}^2); specify what a_i is; either state the bound conditionally on the previously computed columns or lower-bound ||a_i||_2 deterministically (using monotonicity of the noncentral F in the noncentrality); define w_i.
issues.overall_effect: The final QR-under-noise corollary's probability guarantee is wrong or ill-defined as stated, independently of the errors it inherits from thm:noise-ls and cor-main.
issues.title: cor:added-2: wrong degrees of freedom (off by one) and unconditioned application of cor-main to random quantities
issues.why_classification: The product-form conclusion survives, but establishing it requires correcting the indices and supplying a missing conditional-probability argument plus a deterministic noncentrality bound: a contained yet nontrivial rewrite.
